title: Ideal Control System
header: transfer-stage-unified, target architecture, drafted 2026-09-21 against mvc-refactor at 91b5dc9
owner_rulings: Closing a model's tab destructs the model and releases its port; reopening constructs it. No hide/show state.
Autonomous mode stays; Step must work repeatedly inside it.
Scripts / G-code are not used at the station: purged.
Every model has its own estop toggle; the Controller's global FULL STOP is those toggles wired together.
The Web view is localhost only.
The Red Percent CSV analysis plot stays, in all three views, rendered once by the model.
All four gamepad layouts and all three probe types are in service.

hierarchy.text: app.main() picks a view, builds the one Controller and a Setup panel, and opens the view. Nothing else constructs anything.
Setup scans ports and gamepads, validates the assignment and constructs Models into the Controller. It is a Panel, so each view renders it from its schema: one wizard, not three.
A Model owns its Devices (SerialPort, Gamepad, SMC100, Screen). Model.open() and Model.close() open and close them on demand. Model.state reports every Device's status upward in one snapshot.

The Controller owns the Models. add() constructs, remove() estops, closes and destructs. run(name, command, inputs) is the only way a command reaches a model. estop_all() is the per-model estops wired together.

A view holds the Controller and nothing else. It reads schema(name) and state(name) and calls run(). It cannot have a feature the schema does not declare, which is what makes parity the default rather than a goal.
Models and the Controller publish to the one EventLog. Views subscribe. Only EventLog.error may ask for an acknowledged popup, and it is reserved for failed commands, faults and unconfirmed stops.
The browser heartbeat is watched by WebView alone. On silence while Controller.is_active, it calls Controller.estop_all(). No model knows a browser exists.

import_rules: views import Controller, Result, schema helpers and EventLog. Never a Model or a Device.
Models import Device classes, Param, schema and EventLog. Never a view, never the Controller.
Only SerialPort imports pyserial; only GamepadHub imports pygame; only Screen imports mss.
Only Setup constructs Models; only the Controller destructs them.
These four rules are one import-graph test. They replace the Protocol and mixin 'contract' classes.
naming_rules: Properties are nouns and take no parentheses: mode, position, state, schema, series.
Boolean properties start with is_, has_, can_ or needs_: is_open, is_estopped, has_unsaved_data, can_kill_coils.
No get_ prefix anywhere. No _flag, _var or _status suffixes.

Commands are bare imperative verbs, and one verb means one thing on every class: open/close (devices and models), enable/disable (energize), halt (stop motion, no latch), estop/clear_estop (latched), start_run/end_run.
set_<thing>(value) for every operator selection: set_mode, set_source, set_region, set_sync, set_gate.
Private helpers are _verb_noun. Threads are _<x>_thread, their bodies _<x>_loop.
Callbacks a class receives are on_<event>; UI handlers are _on_<widget>_<event>.
No abbreviations: auton -> auto, ser -> port, sch -> schema, cnt/sp -> spelled out. 'controller' means only the Controller; a joystick is a Gamepad.
Names fixed by a framework or vendor are exempt and marked: Qt event handlers, the pyserial interface SimulatedPort imitates, SMC100 protocol methods.
